extracted.intended_audience: NLP/AI researchers and practitioners working on patent examination and legal LLMs
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating models that generate full-stage patent Office Actions and applicant rebuttals, modeling the interactive, multi-turn patent examination lifecycle. Benchmarking should support realistic evaluation settings (oracle and retrieval-simulated) and compare different model classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-stage patent examination lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Models the full patent examination lifecycle, including Office Action generation and applicant rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The benchmark should not treat patent examination as a single-step classification/extraction problem but cover the end-to-end, multi-stage process (examiner issues Office Action; applicant crafts rebuttal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive, multi-turn justification and response
rubrics_metrics.description: Reframes patent examination as a dynamic, multi-turn process of justification and response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should capture iterative interaction between examiner and applicant, assessing coherence across turns, the quality of justifications, and whether responses appropriately address prior objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oracle vs retrieval-simulated evaluation settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports both oracle and retrieval-simulated evaluation settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evaluation under idealized (oracle) conditions and under more realistic retrieval-based pipelines to measure robustness to imperfect information access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world case coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a dataset of authentic examination records to ensure realism; dataset size and provenance matter for ecological validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of technical expertise and legal reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examination is a complex, multi-stage process requiring both technical expertise and legal reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks and evaluations should measure model capabilities in domain-technical understanding and legal-rule application (e.g., novelty, inventive step, claim interpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison between proprietary and open-source models
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal critical insights into model performance, including differences between proprietary and open-source models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include experiments that contrast model families to surface performance gaps and trade-offs attributable to model origin or training/regulatory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task asymmetry between examiner analysis and applicant rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and evaluate task asymmetries between examiner analysis and applicant-side rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat examiner-side generation (finding and articulating objections) and applicant-side rebuttal (responding and arguing) as distinct tasks with potentially different difficulty and evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move beyond discriminative/static extraction benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior benchmarks predominantly view patent examination as discriminative classification or static extraction, failing to capture its inherently interactive and iterative nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design benchmarks that avoid solely discriminative or extraction tasks and instead emphasize generative, sequential, and dialog-like evaluation where justification and counter-argumentation are central.
